lesson.title: Tout le conditionnel
lesson.subtitle: Building any conditional from the future stem + imparfait ending (-ais, -ait).

hook.title: The Full Would-World: Building Any Conditional in Two Seconds
hook.content: Take the infinitive (parler, visiter) or a core r-stem (ser-, aur-, ir-, fer-, voudr-, pourr-) and attach the imparfait endings (-ais, -ais, -ait)! And to build a hypothetical 'If I had..., I would...' sentence: after si ('if'), use the IMPARFAIT (Si j'avais le temps), and in the result clause use the CONDITIONAL (j'irais à Paris)!

footnotes.title: Notice how English does the EXACT same thing in 'If I HAD time, I WOULD go'!
footnotes.content: Si j'avais (imparfait) le temps, j'irais (conditional) à Paris matches English 'If I had time, I would go' 1-for-1!

pattern.title: Si + Imparfait (-ais/-ait) → Conditional (-rais/-rait)
pattern.content: Use the imparfait after si and the conditional in the main clause.
pattern.linguist_note: Counterfactual conditional sentences in French pair an imperfect indicative protasis with a conditional apodosis.
pattern.trap_note: Never put -rais right after si ('Les si n'aiment pas les -rais') — use the imparfait after si!

exercises.prompt: Match each conditional form or si-clause with its meaning:

matching_pairs.german: I would love / I would like

exercises.target_answer: I would love / I would like, I would go, it would be, If I had the time..., ...I would visit Paris
exercises.meaning: j'aimerais (aimer + ais), j'irais (ir- + ais), ce serait (ser- + ait), Si j'avais le temps... (si + imparfait), ...je visiterais Paris (conditional)
exercises.explanation: Imparfait after si; Conditional (-r- + -ais/-ait) in the result clause!

exercises.prompt: Complete the hypothetical sentence: 'If I had time, I would go to the cinema':
options: Si j'avais le temps, j'irais au cinéma
Si j'ai le temps, j'irais au cinéma
Si j'aurais le temps, j'irais au cinéma
exercises.target_answer: Si j'avais le temps, j'irais au cinéma
exercises.explanation: After si, use imparfait j'avais; in the result clause, use conditional j'irais!

exercises.prompt: Build the conditional 'it would be' from the future stem 'ser-' of être + '-ait':

exercises.idea: it would be very good to visit Lyon (use Ce serait très bon de visiter Lyon)
cues: It would be very good → Ce serait très bon
to visit Lyon → de visiter Lyon
idea_parts: conditional pointer → Ce serait très bon
exercises.target_answer: Ce serait très bon de visiter Lyon
exercises.meaning: It would be very good to visit Lyon
exercises.explanation: Ce serait ('it would be') vs. Ce sera ('it will be').

diagnosis.cue: Use conditional Ce serait ('it would be').

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: J'aimerais beaucoup visiter cette ville avec toi
exercises.target_answer: J'aimerais beaucoup visiter cette ville avec toi
exercises.meaning: I would love to visit this city with you
exercises.explanation: J'aimerais beaucoup + bare infinitive is a warm alternative to Je voudrais.
exercises.affirmation: You wrote J'aimerais beaucoup visiter cleanly.

summary.outcome: Form the conditional across regular and irregular verbs and build 'Si + imparfait → conditional' hypothetical sentences.

use_example.german: Si j'habitais à Paris, j'irais au musée tous les dimanches.
use_example.english: If I lived in Paris, I would go to the museum every Sunday.

summary.takeaway: After si ('if') use the imparfait (Si j'avais); in the result use the conditional (j'irais).
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([5111] Dormant Consonants Wake Up): see how Tout le conditionnel leads directly into Dormant Consonants Wake Up.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "It would be very good to visit Lyon" in French:
twist.target_answer: Ce serait très bon de visiter Lyon
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Ce serait très bon de visiter Lyon" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of Tout le conditionnel.

voudrais.context_phrase: Je voudrais un croissant, s'il vous plaît.
voudrais.context_translation: I would like a croissant, please.
voudrais.etymology_derivation: Future stem voudr- + imparfait ending -ais = the polite conditional!

aller.context_translation: I'm going to go to the café.
aller.etymology_derivation: Latin ambulāre 'to walk' → ambler → aller. To go is a stroll away — and the near future rides on it.

avoir.etymology_derivation: Latin habēre = have. The H dropped and stayed dropped — French never pronounces its Latin H.

être.etymology_derivation: Latin esse 'to be' → essere → être. English kept the root in essence and quintessential — the being-ness inside the word.

visiter.etymology_derivation: visitation → visiter. The rare English noun unlocks the everyday verb: don't decide too quickly that you can't say it.

aimé.etymology_derivation: aimer ← ad + estimare 'to estimate'. English 'aim' drifted from the same estimate — aiming is assessing.
